messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty alert: elevated 5xx rate and packet loss observed from inference fleet in eu-central-1a (affecting g5 instances). Start triage.
alana: seeing ~30% request egress failures from eu-central-1a to model-serving pods, p95 latency spiking. Customers on Dedicated capacity reporting timeouts.
mike: I can confirm — host-level metrics show increasing network retransmits on a subset of ENIs. Not all instances. Starting to gather instance IDs.
sylvia: tagging the impacted instances in the console now. If this is zonal networking (AZ-local) we should consider routing to eu-central-1b and eu-central-1c.
devon: paging note: aws health dashboard flags "network impairment" for eu-central-1a? I'm seeing a degraded status for that AZ in status.aws.amazon.com (third-party feed) but not official RCAs yet.
alana: good call on cross-AZ routing. We have automatic fallback but traffic is skewed to that AZ because of sticky subnets and a recent scale-up. Need immediate manual reroute to avoid customer impact.
eng-sre: proposed mitigation steps: 1) set route53 failover weight to divert 70% of inference traffic to eu-central-1b/c endpoints, 2) trigger warm-standby pool in eu-central-1b (spin g5 alternatives), 3) reduce model shard memory config to allow more instances to fit on warm nodes.
mike: I can update Route53 weights. Quick sanity: current TTL is 60s, so changes propagate quickly.
sylvia: can we also shift Canary / canary-routing to fallback models? Some customers are pinned to specific endpoints — we need per-customer routing overrides in the console.
devon: I'm on customer overrides now — adding customer_tag override for big-tier customers to route to eu-central-1b endpoints. Doing in console: POST /routing/overrides {"customer":"big-corp","region":"eu-central-1b"}
alana: runbook note: if we change weights, remember to keep health checks in failover mode. Health-checkers currently run from eu-west-1; they will see degraded and automatic failover might already be in play but not fully triggered because several nodes still pass.
incident-bot: @pagerduty new incident created: INC-2026-0423-07. severity: high. On-call: @mike.
mike: starting manual weight shift now. Updating Route53 records:
```
# set weights for inference endpoints
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-central-1b","Weight":700,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"35.180.1.12"}]}}]}'
```
alana: deploying warm-standby instances in 1b: using existing AMI + reduced model config. Launch command:
```
./deploy/warm_pool --region eu-central-1b --instance-type g5.4xlarge --image ami-0abcd --model-config small-shard
```
sylvia: customers reporting partial failures via support. CS has posted the public status update draft to #customer-communications. We should coordinate messaging after mitigation steps.
devon: updated routing overrides for 3 enterprise tenants. Confirmed traffic redirected.
mike: Route53 change submitted. Observability shows traffic shifting away from 1a over the next minute. p95 latency dropping for rerouted requests.
alana: still seeing some 5xxs from existing long-lived connections to 1a. Might be connection teardown / TCP resets. We should terminate stuck connections on load balancers for 1a target groups.
eng-sre: running command to deregister targets in ALB target group for eu-central-1a:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-1a/abcd --targets Id=i-0abcde
```
mike: deregistered a handful. Health checks returning 504 for some targets then marking unhealthy. Traffic now routing to 1b/c.
incident-bot: update: mitigation progress 40% — cross-AZ reroute in effect, warm-standby spin-up underway.
sylvia: note: autoscaling in 1b created 6 warm nodes but some failed due to ENI attach limit in the subnet. Workaround: increase ENI quota or use larger instance types to reduce per-node count.
devon: changing launch config to use g5.8xlarge (fewer nodes required). Re-launching.
mike: monitoring customer errors: big-corp still seeing intermittent timeouts — looks like their traffic was pinned to some cached endpoints at CDN layer. CS to reach out to them for a brief DNS cache flush suggestion.
alana: starting rolling restart of fleet agents to drop stuck connections in 1a. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-nodes -n eu-central-1a`
eng-sre: restart kicked off. Expect brief ephemeral errors for in-flight sessions.
devon: warm pool in 1b now up with smaller-shard models. We routed enterprise customers to those pods. Observability shows successful inference responses.
mike: AWS health now shows increased API errors for EC2 in eu-central-1a. Filing AWS support ticket: case 87654321.
incident-bot: @eng-sre on-call handover scheduled in 30 minutes. Current assignee: mike -> sylvia.
sylvia: taking handoff. Summary: networking degradation in eu-central-1a causing packet loss and elevated retransmits on g5 hosts. Cross-AZ failover applied via Route53 weights and ALB deregistration. Warm-standby in 1b handling traffic. Next actions: monitor for AZ recovery and scale down warm pool when stable.
alana: customer impact: 12 enterprise customers impacted with increased latency/timeouts; we contacted top 5 via CS with mitigation notes. Public status: minor outage for certain regions — posting now.
sylvia: posting status update: "We are experiencing a degraded network condition affecting eu-central-1a which may cause elevated latency and timeouts for inference requests. Traffic is being redirected to other AZs; we are working with AWS."
incident-bot: status update published to status.redwood.com.
mike: adding timeline notes to the incident doc and linking to logs.
eng-sre: recommended root-cause hypotheses: 1) AZ-local networking hardware or fabric issue causing retransmits, 2) noisy neighbor exhausting ENI throughput, 3) routing flap in provider backbone. Need AWS confirmation.
devon: AWS support acknowledged receipt and escalated to internal network team. ETA unknown.
alana: monitoring will continue. If AWS doesn't provide clear RCA in 2 hours, we should move enterprise customers to eu-west-1 cold standby and open a post-incident review.
sylvia: agreed. For now, mitigation stands. I'll update the incident channel with any changes.
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-0423-07 transition to status: mitigated (partial). Further updates in this thread.
